Semuc Champey is known for the natural pools above the course of the Cahabón River. The river disappears beneath a natural limestone bridge before emerging again at the surface. Above the underground section, water forms separate basins and small cascades that together create an unusual river landscape.

The water ranges in color from green to blue. The surrounding vegetation adds to the views of the pools and places this natural complex within a humid forest region. Semuc Champey is visited from the Cobán area. What makes it remarkable is the combination of the river's underground course and the open chain of pools above it.

## Cienfuegos — the "Pearl of Southern Cuba"

Cienfuegos is the capital of the province of the same name on the Caribbean coast. The city was founded by French immigrants in 1819 under the name Fernandina de Jagua. It received its current name in 1880. The city stands on the shore of a beautiful bay, and the sea is central to much of its character.

Cienfuegos preserves one of Cuba's most architecturally coherent city centers, filled with classical facades and slender columns. Together they evoke the atmosphere of 19th-century France, which inspired the city's design.

## Cienfuegos — a UNESCO World Heritage Site!

Cienfuegos is a city open to the sea, built around Cuba's largest bay. Its maritime atmosphere is unmistakable, while its restored streets give the city a sense of calm. In 2005, it was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. One of its most notable landmarks is José Martí Park, surrounded by beautiful buildings with rich histories. The park contains Cuba's only triumphal arch, as well as a theater, a cathedral, and palaces.

In Serra da Bocaina National Park, mountain forest meets the coast. Nature routes explore rivers, waterfalls, and forest trails.

Near Trindade lies the park's coastal section, with beaches and a natural pool among the rocks. The closeness of forest and ocean reveals different landscapes within a single natural area.

Shelter Bay lies near the Caribbean entrance to the Panama Canal. The bay is associated with a yacht marina and sea journeys between the two sides of Panama. After navigating the canal, vessels return here to coastal routes and island destinations.

The local marina offers a glimpse of everyday life at a yachting harbor: vessels at the docks, shore services, and sheltered waters. Shelter Bay adds a maritime landscape to the engineering experience of the canal. From this part of the coast, journeys continue toward the Caribbean islands of San Blas.

Sicuani is a town in the Vilcanota Valley on the road between Cusco and Puno. It serves as an intermediate stop on a longer Andean itinerary, marking a shift between visits to archaeological sites and the journey onward to high-altitude landscapes.

Exploring Sicuani offers a view of everyday urban life beyond the region's main tourist centers. Low-rise buildings and the surrounding mountain slopes maintain the town's connection to the valley. On transfer itineraries, Sicuani is often used as a lunch stop.
